svg.title: ATLAS device: main circuit diagram
svg.desc: KiCad-style schematic of the ATLAS Wokwi circuit: ESP32 DevKit V1 with all 30 pins, three LEDs through 220 ohm resistors, two push-buttons, a simulated GNSS receiver on UART2, the serial monitor and the simulated Wi-Fi path. Generated from firmware/atlas_device/diagram.json. Simulated in Wokwi, not built on physical hardware.

g.text: dual-core Xtensa LX6 · 240 MHz · Wi-Fi 2.4 GHz · Bluetooth
on board: USB-UART → TX0/RX0 · 3.3 V LDO VIN → 3V3 · EN + BOOT buttons

svg.text: Wi-Fi path (simulated, all on this machine)
SW1 / SW2 return → GND.1 (buttons are active low: INPUT_PULLUP, a press reads LOW)
1 All GND pins are one net on the DevKit. As wired in
diagram.json, the LEDs return through GND.2 and the
2 SW1 and SW2 are active low: INPUT_PULLUP holds the pin
HIGH, a press pulls it to GND.
3 LED current I = (3.3 V − V_F) / 220 Ω; a red LED at
4 GPIO12 (SEND) is a boot strapping pin. The button pulls
it LOW, which is its safe level at boot.
5 ADC2 pins cannot read analog while Wi-Fi is on; ATLAS
uses its ADC2 pins as digital I/O only.
6 ✕ marks a pin with nothing connected (18 of 30).
7 LEDs: green = ALLOW; amber = STEP_UP, DELAY or PENDING;
red = DENY, FAIL_CLOSED or any unrecognised reply.
8 U2 is a SIMULATED GNSS receiver (a Wokwi custom
chip): NMEA on UART2, scripted positions, no satellites.
Its GND joins the one ground net.
Simulated in Wokwi · not built on physical hardware
